Document 317
Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume XI,
                    South Asia Crisis, 1971
317. Memorandum for the Record
1
Washington
,
December 16, 1971
.
Shortly after 10:00 a.m. this morning General
Haig
called on the secure line to say the following:
The President wishes Mr.
Sisco
to call
                        in Indian Ambassador
Jha
immediately.
Sisco
should make the following
                        three points forcefully.
1.
With respect to Indiaʼs earlier refusal to give assurances that it had
                            no territorial ambitions without similar assurances from Pakistan, we
                            are now giving him Pak assurances of no territorial ambitions. We wish
                            to know immediately that India has no territorial ambitions on its
                            side.
2.
Now that East Pakistan has fallen, there can be no justification for
                            continued fighting. If fighting continues, it will “have the most
                            drastic consequences on
U.S.
-Indian
                            relations.” (
Haig
commented
                            that we should be no more specific than that.)
3.
We consider it intolerable for the Indian Ambassador to use our media
                            as a platform to make attacks on the
U.S.
Government.
2
RHM
Deputy Executive Secretary
